title: Steampunk Sewing Machine
content:
## _"Marvelous Designer is a fantastically powerful software to accomplish different cloth stitching, seams, and sim situations."_

* * *

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HG-CWk2HvbE

# **Interview with Jeremy Scharphorn |**[**Steampunk Sewing Machine**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/8wyEoQ)**| 3D Environment and Prop Artist**

* * *

# **Artist Introduction**

Hey! I'm Jeremy and I'm based in the U.S. I am a self-taught 3D Environment and Prop artist. I found out rather quickly that many indie companies combine the roles of a level and environment designer. I had zero ideas how to make anything 3D, but was determined to make any environment I could imagine! Fast-forward a few years and I'm still learning tons in 3D and receiving some game design gigs alongside art ones, but my heart is in environments and props! 

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/24dd2dfa082541eba88fbfbd1aa58644/images/bf7dcb5084dd476394238c4d5de4c45csweing%20machine1.png)

As an environment and prop artist, my cloth needs are a bit different than say, a character artists. As such, Blender has been an alright software for me for these past years since my cloth sim needs have been quite minimal. Though as my skills are going deeper into the intermediate range and as I'm shooting for that coveted "expert" skill set, I am switching to more industry standard tools that pack that extra punch that my work could really use. I'm still rather new to Marvelous Designer and ZBrush, but one rather common pipeline I have seen and am enjoying is using Marvelous Designer for cloth sims and then bringing it into ZBrush for finer sculpting as needed. Though I should confess, with the short time I had left to complete the competition I did skip the ZBrush step and went straight to Substance Painter. The additional fold details were all painted on procedurally with some extra manual adjustments as needed. For a photorealistic piece I would not recommend this route if time permits, but if you're crunched for time like I was, or are doing a stylized piece, skipping the ZBrush step and using Substance Painter is great as well. If I were to do it again I would create everything in Marvelous Designer and refine it as needed in ZBrush.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/24dd2dfa082541eba88fbfbd1aa58644/images/5f80ba749a6847008b8f1eb2d47ca40fsweing%202.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/24dd2dfa082541eba88fbfbd1aa58644/images/842965ed7ba34670ab53ff25eb2e7169sweing%203.png)

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

Marvelous designer is a fantastically powerful software. I am constantly surprised while working in it how relatively simple it is to accomplish different cloth stitching, seams, and sim situations. I already knew Marvelous Designer was an amazing software, but when working under that time pressure I was really shown how amazing it can be. Within a few hours, I had exactly what I wanted with no other production experience in the software and certainly no pipeline integration experience with it. Marvelous Designer gave me so much more control than any other software or add-ons could and learning it was incredibly easy! I highly recommend it to anyone, including environment artists, as it just can’t be beat!

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/24dd2dfa082541eba88fbfbd1aa58644/images/55c11cdd94fb4fb4a8556db7166c6b21swring%204.png)

by **Jeremy Scharphorn**

[**Artstation**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/8wyEoQ)
content_description: Discover how 3D artist Jeremy Scharphorn leverages Marvelous Designer’s intuitive cloth simulation tools to create detailed and realistic environment props with ease and efficiency.

title: Cyberpunk Nightclub Storage Props
content:
## _A 3D Environment Artist, Furkan adapted Marvelous Designer to make a realistic effect with PVC cloth on the table._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/94f8993d0c5049ffbf6be357dcfa6308/images/bb5a8e65382942918fd26571c035f64acyberpunk%20nightclub1.png)

# **Interview with Mehmet Furkan Malli |**[**Cyberpunk Nightclub Storage Props**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/Ar54BN)

* * *

# **Artist Introduction**

Hello, my name is Furkan. I’m a 3D Environment Artist working in the game development industry for not so long. I studied architecture in college and it was a pivotal moment for me to realize that I could apply my design knowledge such as form, colour, light and most obviously creating spaces to game art. I have started my game art journey by working on props by interpreting real-life references. Creating multiple props and arranging them in a plausible way was the next step for me, as I have tried to accomplish for this challenge. It’s still an ongoing process for me; creating environments and learning game engines to tell a story. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/94f8993d0c5049ffbf6be357dcfa6308/images/6c038fcf084741619555e93effbcbbb7nighclub2.png.png)

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

After I decide on what to do, I always start with gathering references. I use PureRef to bring together the images I choose. After that, I start to work with blocks and simple geometries. It’s important to see proportions and make it look like how you planned from the beginning. Maya and Blender are my modelling tools for creating low-poly models. Although I could use those tools for high poly, I love how ZBrush can make it easier to create high poly models. In order to bake high poly details to low poly models, Marmoset Toolbag is a very smooth and fast option on my pipeline. For this challenge, I used Marvelous Designer to strengthen the Cyberpunk feeling and overall look. It was easy for me to imagine the cloth and materials when considering Cyberpunk Theme. It was a transparent PVC cloth I had seen on Blade Runner many times, and I knew I could easily simulate and export a single sheet of PVC cloth in Marvelous Designer. After all of these, my favourite part begins which is texturing and Substance Painter, the one and only tool that works for me. Finally to make a portfolio presentation I go back to Marmoset Toolbag for some renders.

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

I could say it was an enjoyable and fun process for me. Dragging and pulling the cloth so easily is genuinely entertaining. I could say it was easy to use for me, of course, I’m not creating complex clothing or using it for fashion purposes. However, Marvelous Designer is going to be a great tool for me, as an environment artist, I’m not going to hesitate a second to use it for my scene and won’t bother myself with modelling tools to create cloth pieces. 

by **Mehmet Furkan Malli**

[**Artstation**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/Ar54BN)
content_description: Showcasing 3D Environment Artist Mehmet Furkan Malli’s creative process and innovative use of Marvelous Designer to craft realistic PVC cloth effects for cyberpunk-themed game environments.

content:
## _To express detailed wrinkles, but most easily, Marvelous Designer is irreplaceable. Read how he uniquely created the Nightclub seat._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/db9706ce80b446a6a70bbfc4730411a2/images/1f6ed3b291d24a86847709c93241367b012f4a80ceeb4da7a528d298d5e61129.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/db9706ce80b446a6a70bbfc4730411a2/images/ccd98fdd886a4ad8bc178800bae497fa1a46c0803777420ea62546068235994b.png)

# **An Interview from Monthly 3D Prop Challenge: Leartes Studios X Marvelous Designer - Cyberpunk**

**Learn more about this challenge and be the next special prize winner! (**[**LINK**](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/discover/news/view/115)**)**

* * *

# **1\. Artist Introduction**

My name is Filip Steć. I am a 3D artist with 5 years of experience. I live in Warsaw, Poland and work in the games industry. I usually do environments, but I like trying other things connected with 3D game art. That’s why I participated in Leartes Studios X Marvelous Designer challenge. 

# **2\. Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

I find my pipeline quite standard - for modelling Maya and Blender, for sculpting ZBrush, for texturing Substance Painter, but I see more and more cases where Marvelous Designer can be irreplaceable. Not only in the case of clothes of course, but even in the environment and prop design, it can bring assets to the next level.

# **3\. How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

Actually, I find myself a beginner in Marvelous Designer. Before my first try with Marvelous Designer, I thought it’s really powerful but demanding and non-flexible software. I couldn’t be more wrong. In fact, **it’s extremely powerful but I was surprised how I can adjust it to my needs.**

* * *

**_by FILIP STEĆ_**

title: Nina Chernyshenko
content:
## ![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/88b575e1f6aa44d48979f46732490525/images/63c70e89d3ba4b8d8d83a731f4448d0cHeader_thumb%20%288%29.png)_Nina opens up our eyes with beautiful historical and fantasy outfits. Check out her invaluable tips to express fine details._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/88b575e1f6aa44d48979f46732490525/images/9a1618f222b8420290ccaa24c8cacb814b86f8386a004bed9d3d0b4b156ecab0.jpg)

# **Interview with Nina Chernyshenko**

* * *

# **1\. Artist Introduction**

Hello, my name is Nina. I'm from Ukraine, and I'm a freelance digital artist focusing on creating digital clothing. I especially like to make historical clothes and clothes from movies. And I have a digital clothing store on ArtStation.

# **2\. When did you start to learn Marvelous Designer, and what motivated you to start in the first place?**

I started out with 2D and most of all I liked to draw characters. But then I thought that it would be interesting to see my characters from all angles, and I decided to start mastering 3D programs. I've watched a lot of YouTube channels about 3D. And one day I came across a tutorial about clothes creation in Marvelous Designer (sometime in 2018). And it turned out to be my dream program. I've always enjoyed drawing and sewing clothes. And I realized that I want to grow in this direction with Marvelous Designer's help.

# **3\. How do you start with your design in Marvelous Designer?**

Before I start creating clothes in Marvelous Designer, I pick up a lot of references and save them in PureRef. I find references on Pinterest, Instagram, or just Google. [In the Marvelous Designer Discord channel **(LINK)**](https://discord.com/invite/HAh568h) also has a pattern-reference section with links to sites where you can find interesting patterns. If I want to make a garment with a complicated design, I try to find a pattern-reference. If I make a historical costume, I also look for patterns to make the clothes as authentic as possible. And if I find a pattern, I import it into the 2D window and trace it with the Polygon tool. But even with this method, you have to adapt the patterns to your avatar. Especially for historical clothes, since historical clothes are based on people of that time and their body parameters differ from standard Marvelous Designer or DAZ Studio avatars. You can use **Modular Configurator** patterns to create modern clothes. 

# **4\. We'd like to see your favorite artworks. Please introduce them to us!**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/88b575e1f6aa44d48979f46732490525/images/7cfde363fdd54b7eb927437b4bd340f54b86f8386a004bed9d3d0b4b156ecab0.jpg)

My favorites are, of course, historical clothing and fantasy outfits. It's my passion. There are many interesting challenges in creating historic dresses. For example, how to give the right shape to the skirt.

This can be done in the following ways:

**[Skirt Part]**

1\. Model the frame in any 3D program (Blender, Zbrush) and then import it into Marvelous Designer as an avatar.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/88b575e1f6aa44d48979f46732490525/images/899c8087687343ea9031bc3823294e06aa768725bb9f4bc28e411bd646aaef3e.jpg)

2\. Create a frame in Marvelous Designer from **stiff fabric (_Trim_Full_Grain_Leather_)** and after giving the desired shape and volume freeze the fabric.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/88b575e1f6aa44d48979f46732490525/images/0ef660f4e72d4bc9b7869c729907cf508fc28e11e3a74177a9f659f11ef02b5a.jpg)

3\. Use several ruffled underskirts. Also, an integral part of historical costumes is the corset.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/88b575e1f6aa44d48979f46732490525/images/76b58d6e7bc04f3faefb605b8f441750bbe648dd3f784e84a05ba9f2f5f2d443.jpg)

**[Corset Part]**

1\. I create a base of stiff fabric (**_Trim_Full_Grain_Leather_**). And then, using the function **Layer Clone (Over)** , I create another layer and assign soft material to it (_Knit_Cotton_Rayon Jersey or Nylon_Featherweight_) and set **Particle Distance 5**.

2\. To add more realism, for the top layer, increase **the Shrinkage Weft and Warp** parameters. The simulation will show more folds. [You can download the corset file for free here (**LINK**).](https://www.artstation.com/a/4328688)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/88b575e1f6aa44d48979f46732490525/images/b8f34688500040cba64cfcc7655530df99cb3680ac4c4f87b6a6fe4eb50f95c4.jpg)

**[Accessory Part]**

Also, in my projects I often add various accessories made in Blender. These are gems that I import as trims or register as buttons, buckles, knives, swords, sabers.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/88b575e1f6aa44d48979f46732490525/images/0a934938b7cc441eb9d74d0070e605e4253572b188af480b937c4ccea97e5cd5.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/88b575e1f6aa44d48979f46732490525/images/dc778ec0d38b48278e2fe296154a4ab471459693a6d24c29b6d525ee93670b5c.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/88b575e1f6aa44d48979f46732490525/images/d801972929f74b73a2e288913bfb4b0e7b6156f9424d487fb8d2c03260c1f940.jpg)

When you import objects into Marvelous Designer as **Trims** , these objects will move with the fabric when simulating the garment. If you import them as Avatar, they will have to be moved manually. Also pay attention to the properties of these objects in the Property Editor, such as Skin Offset, Static and Kinetic Friction, Weight and Collision. I make hats, bags and shoes in Marvelous Designer. For this purpose, I mostly use the _Trim_Full_Grain_Leather and Leather_Lambskin presets_. To create the curves of the shape help **internal lines** (indicating a certain bending angle) and Tack. And it's also important to select the necessary angle of stitching patterns.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/88b575e1f6aa44d48979f46732490525/images/27e492c92b0d4f83a553bb5036b95e9bdc5fb3b7ac6e483a88880dc7b1998fb3.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/88b575e1f6aa44d48979f46732490525/images/c103a7a019764097aa64703e3652483267f65f2fff354ccfaf61ea42b2e41d2b.jpg)

# **5\. Can you tell us your process for one of the artworks, including how you used Marvelous Designer and other tools?**

I use standard free avatars from DAZ Studio (Daz_Genesis 8 female, male). I export the avatar in **A-pose** in COLLADA format**(.dae)**. In Marvelous Designer there are several avatar settings. If you want your clothes to fit more closely to the avatar, set **Skin Offset 1 or 0.** If you want your clothes not to slide on the avatar, increase the Static and Kinetic Friction settings. I also usually smooth out the avatar.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/88b575e1f6aa44d48979f46732490525/images/f6034e8280434c72a490363a30542d5bbec0e881eff84f35b5dbd7601e2c6809.jpg)

I build basic patterns. I don't use the measurements on the avatar when I build it, I build it by eye. And then I adjust it to the avatar. First, I make the base of the corset and the skirt. I use a tack on the avatar in the center of the corset, so the corset would fit better to the avatar. Dividing the bodice into four parts helps to fit the bodice to the shape of the breasts.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/88b575e1f6aa44d48979f46732490525/images/033e1e590d134ac5b76312eab17ec78d576914d955c14d58961bd7f5953429f8.jpg)

I select the lines where the sleeve is sewn (armhole) and set **Elastic Ratio=100** for strength.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/88b575e1f6aa44d48979f46732490525/images/b56c19eb58514166afe160569b7e068f9f02d6fd6494413698f053a1392b808a.jpg)

With the help of Layer Clone Over I duplicate the shoulder pad. With the help of inner lines, I form the ribs. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/88b575e1f6aa44d48979f46732490525/images/463031cd41484502ae2f5ce5e1897f20119e2e0e14f44f71a9a5cbdb4bbcb08a.jpg)

When the dress is ready I set Particle Distance 5 for all parts of the dress, and 3 for the smaller parts (buttonholes and pattern).

I pose the avatar in DAZ Studio and export it in COLLADA format **(.dae)**. I import it into Marvelous Designer. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/88b575e1f6aa44d48979f46732490525/images/bc603ca41c3c436499376cc14009fa1af4ab7eb664394686ba56600a9d896eee.jpg)

I save it as **A pose**.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/88b575e1f6aa44d48979f46732490525/images/a7af3556e9c642babc3b27d0115057ce916f4bb492ff49e39eee54a7de234ab6.jpg)

Then I delete the imported avatar. You can set **Particle Distance 15** for all patterns, for faster simulation. Then I open the saved pose. [You can download the fantasy dress file here (**LINK**).](https://www.artstation.com/a/12693295.)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/88b575e1f6aa44d48979f46732490525/images/f1df679283af4d11a683fe5a8b67d71d7146cf663035444fab598ce73ae12ccc.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/88b575e1f6aa44d48979f46732490525/images/abbb4c92027e4393b6fa06e1af65933c86ee4fc1aaba4198a425b59105a9484f.jpg)

# **6\. For the Marvelous Designer NEW learners, can you give any tips or advice?**

The Marvelous Designer program is not difficult to master. All the necessary information about interface and functionality is on the Marvelous Designer's [**YouTube**](https://www.youtube.com/user/marvelousdesigner3)channel. With each new tutorial you watch, it will become easier and easier for you to use the program.**Marvelous Designer is an indispensable assistant in creating realistic clothes for your characters and in interior design.**

* * *

**By Nina Chernyshenko**

** _Link to_**[** _Instagram_**](https://www.instagram.com/nini_chernyshenko/)

** _Link to_**[** _ArtStation_**](https://www.artstation.com/sninoka)
content_description: This page showcases digital artist Nina Chernyshenko’s expertise in creating detailed historical and fantasy clothing using Marvelous Designer, offering insights, process tips, and downloadable resources for aspiring 3D garment creators.

title: FAITH & HONOUR: BARBAROSSA
content:
## _FAITH & HONOUR: BARBAROSSA, a historically authentic Adventure RPG set, complete characters' outfits with Marvelous Designer. Check out the whole pipeline they adopted._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5ea73f5d40b649288c6468191cdd7b53/images/4b6d48779de34e47890dabb93a928397%EC%8A%A4%ED%81%AC%EB%A6%B0%EC%83%B7%202025-01-14%20113851.png)

# **Interview with Encurio GmbH**

* * *

# **1\. Could you introduce your team and recent project - FAITH & HONOUR: BARBAROSSA?**

Encurio GmbH was founded in 1995 as a marketing company and begun developing video games in 2013. Our studio is located in Cologne, Germany. Our first game, Valnir Rok, was released in 2017.

Currently we are working on our new Game called ** _FAITH & HONOUR: _BARBAROSSA**. It's a historically authentic Adventure RPG set in the 12th century, during the crusade of Frederick I. Barbarossa.

You play as Ulrich, the son of Mathis Reinhardt who was one of Barbarossa’s closest friends until he fell from grace after betraying the emperor. But you know that your father wasn’t a traitor to the Holy Roman Empire and through joining Barbarossa’s crusade you try to find out what really happened while your father was in the emperor’s service.

# **2\. How is Marvelous Designer integrated into your pipeline?**

Since our current project is very ambitious, and we need to make many historically authentic garments, Marvelous Designer has been and is essential to our character art pipeline.

I got an internship as a character artist at Encurio in 2018. Since then, I have been struggling with the internal work pipeline. I took CGMA's "Cloth Simulation for Games" course with Laura Gallagher in mid 2020 to have a decent foundation with Marvelous Designer and also a better understanding of my craft. Laura has now built her own learning platform to teach Character Artists the necessary knowledge. For anyone who wants to learn Marvelous Designer for working in the game industry, I can only recommend [https://outgang.studio](https://outgang.studio). Our Character Pipeline is very similar to Laura's recommended CharacterArt Pipeline. The idea behind Laura Gallaghers workflow is to use a virtual reconstruction technique, that is used in the real life fashion industry.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5ea73f5d40b649288c6468191cdd7b53/images/d1453d683b70443ba2a5529b691617af4d57acc1075a445b8b662c2b9c3bbd65.png)

You start in ZBrush and sketch the garment with Dynamesh, so it perfectly fits the body like in your references. Afterwards, you split the garment in multiple polygroups, where you would have seams. Then you ZRemesh the garment and can export the mesh for the next step.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5ea73f5d40b649288c6468191cdd7b53/images/f844b9afcaea487e8e9f37eee1737d73f9c66f8cd2234a4eaca9e62dd4958e0c.png)

After import, you just UV the mesh inside maya to get a 2D layout, which will later be our pattern. This mesh can now be exported once again and is ready to be imported into marvelous as our new garment. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5ea73f5d40b649288c6468191cdd7b53/images/72df437d38bb47798fba1e502308776f96fb0b745cc44e9999b705e27fec1995.png)

We can import our mesh from obj to a garment and enable "Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map". This will create the patterns from our UVs. This is the stage, where we need to iterate a lot to have a "perfect" fit for our garment. We adjust the Sketch in ZBrush, adjust the UVs ... export, import "OBJ to Garment" .... and repeat. It`s much easier to fix fitting issues on the Sketch than in Marvelous.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5ea73f5d40b649288c6468191cdd7b53/images/75652d70c85e4cb7899e38955ada77cf506e1952b1c2472586ea65cda56132b1.png)

When the garment is fitting, we can continue to work on the details. We crank up the particle distance, add borders and trims and work on the material/folds properties. After the final simulation, we merge some panels, where we don't want to have space inbetween and change the mesh type from Triangle to Quadrangulated for the final export.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5ea73f5d40b649288c6468191cdd7b53/images/1b807f0c7b95481fa4cdc7ec3b9693cb1fae154b2e6044c59889a7f811a26e1a.png)

Back in ZBrush we load our Garment into our "Modular Character Template" file to check and see, if the garment fits into our modular character system. Here we adjust the shape and add accessories and details. Afterwards we continue with the usual well known retopo process. I like to export the mesh as alembic (.abc) without decimating and import the mesh as alembic in Maya as GPU Cache. Saving tons of time and issues I had in the past with the decimating process. Viewport stays blazing fast, even with millions of polygons inside maya.  


![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5ea73f5d40b649288c6468191cdd7b53/images/430bd5e0dc6d408981ef5d357efbcb3cde28fdbc5161412293576dad029f6e79.png)

We are texturing the garments with a "Material Based Approach" just like in Paragon. Texturing with Substance, Baking with Marmoset Toolbag (<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nVes6OUyzdw>). This allows us to reuse a lot of assets and have a lot of customization option.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5ea73f5d40b649288c6468191cdd7b53/images/1694588cfd8b4c35a6c1814800815bb2d0872e4adac945d0bf249b37dd285e6a.png)

# **3\. What is Marvelous Designer’s strong point to use?**

A way better structured and intuitive workflow, which results in high-quality assets/clothes. Another obvious point is the realistic folds and the very good reusability of garments across projects. Just pushing and pulling the garment during the simulation creates a completely different model from the same patterns. Personally I wouldn't want to work with any other tool than Marvelous Designer.

title: Cyberpunk 2077
content:
## _CD PROJEKT RED team introduces the greatest project-Cyberpunk 2077 and the use of Marvelous Designer to accomplish consistently outstanding for many costumes._

* * *

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qIcTM8WXFjk

# **Interview with CD PROJEKT RED**

* * *

# **1\. Could you introduce the recent project - Cyberpunk 2077 ?**

Cyberpunk 2077 is an open world action role-playing video game developed by CD PROJEKT RED set in Mike Pondsmith’s Cyberpunk universe. In the game, players take on the role of up-and-coming mercenary V, embarking on a violent and dangerous journey through the underbelly of Night City, where body modification via the installation of cyberware is a common part of everyday life.

In terms of art, Cyberpunk 2077 is the most demanding and ambitious project in the studio’s history so far. Night City is populated with characters representing a wide spectrum of society from poverty, gangs, and middle class, to corporation workers, celebrities, and even droids. To fill this world, the character art department had to create hundreds of high quality models to make the city feel as immersive and believable as possible.

# **2\. How is Marvelous Designer integrated in the project pipeline?**

Marvelous Designer is one of the most important tools in our character creation pipeline. Almost all the characters' clothes that you can see in Cyberpunk 2077 were created with help of Marvelous Designer.

It was used not only for character garments but also for some cybernetic parts, backpacks, ammo bags, and even weapons. The main challenge during the creation of models for the game was its futuristic cloth design — for example the jacket worn by the main character V. This jacket combines garments with cyberware, and thanks to Marvelous Designer’s variety of material presets, the ability to sew one cloth layer onto another, and features like**** seam taping, I was able to achieve the desired look.

# **3\. Tell us some tips of patterns making and cloth simulation.**

One of my favorite techniques for making realistic folds is the two layer approach. For the bottom layer I often use firm fabric presets like Leather_Cowhide which is used as a cloth base, while for the top one I'll use softer prestes like Nylon_Featherweight — with slightly increased Shrinkage parameters to finalize folds details. For things like cables, collars, and zippers I recommend using the Trim_Full_Grain_Leather preset which you can export to 3D modeling software and use as a starting point for the final model.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a7f9011def9f4c85bdc073da221a9146/images/afe6e1c360af43059f123044169156521%20%281%29.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a7f9011def9f4c85bdc073da221a9146/images/7b2d6fe7f1f24a40b2f38f41433c3dc42%20%281%29.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a7f9011def9f4c85bdc073da221a9146/images/d5d83003ea5f4ea58621983a129dd8113%20%281%29.png)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a7f9011def9f4c85bdc073da221a9146/images/a2ebc356f4184cb196921fa22354822c6.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a7f9011def9f4c85bdc073da221a9146/images/bfda9e5ee0f249a6ae43a3b4a2affbcd5.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a7f9011def9f4c85bdc073da221a9146/images/877d7f44bd7a4b749f14c6888c444d104.png)

This puffy vest is a great example of how the two layer approach combined with pressure works. In this case I created a simple vest pattern as a base. Layer clone (over), drawing internal lines, and then the cut and sew function were used to create cushioned parts. To achieve a realistic look and finalize the necessary details, I increased shrinkage value and applied some pressure to separate pattern pieces.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a7f9011def9f4c85bdc073da221a9146/images/024d6642b78c4b3eb3732db8b1ae2e247.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a7f9011def9f4c85bdc073da221a9146/images/b1c60e4bba754e688d2198e0cfe304f88.png)

Marvelous Designer has the great ability to edit every single fabric parameter by hand; so the cloth look can be improved even without changing the patterns. In this case the user manual was very helpful for explaining how Bending, Shear, or Buckling works.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a7f9011def9f4c85bdc073da221a9146/images/2e7aaabfdb874de18cc1730f16e2f187c6044a6bd1ad44e1989277f6eb122d81.png)

Another great feature of Marvelous Designer allows the importing of objects as patterns. This is very helpful in cases when you want to combine hard surfaces with cloth. For Cyberpunk 2077, I used this function to create some elements for Adam Smasher’s model — such as the cloth on the pipes, and cloth on his armor plates. To make those pieces, first I created simple models with UV maps, then imported them to Marvelous Designer as Avatar. Secondly, I imported them again but this time using the Load as Garment option with Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map checked on.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a7f9011def9f4c85bdc073da221a9146/images/24088fba74cb474484827d2e93af350f10.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a7f9011def9f4c85bdc073da221a9146/images/e38550e144f04800bdfd19225edac8c711.png)

One of the tricks I use to keep cloth from falling off the avatar is to apply a negative pressure value to the pattern, then freeze it and use Layer Clone (over) so I have a pattern base to start with.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a7f9011def9f4c85bdc073da221a9146/images/8a77538c14de47a19a6d8bfa663e06aa13.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a7f9011def9f4c85bdc073da221a9146/images/eb5d47a28eb74bb9a526116f73108b3f12.png)

The policeman hat model is a good example of how avatars can help with garment creation. Here, using other 3D software I modeled a skeleton/chassis to support the cloth shape, then imported it as Avatar.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a7f9011def9f4c85bdc073da221a9146/images/c4fe0a2f76a54c9dbfcbc5f4dea1f95314.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a7f9011def9f4c85bdc073da221a9146/images/282f3021577349b8b48ab81ff3db6fa015.png)

# **4\. What is Marvelous Designer’s strong point to use?**

Everybody knows how sculpting clothes by hand takes a lot of time and, sometimes, the result is not satisfactory even for the most experienced artists. Marvelous Designer is the solution for that. It's a completely new way of making clothes, it's easy to learn, and the final results can be consistently outstanding.

I would definitely recommend Marvelous Designer to other 3D artists. Using Marvelous Designer is the best way to improve the quality of your models.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a7f9011def9f4c85bdc073da221a9146/images/1ea829d5e3f8441fbd12a6cedb55024099bd4ab6c8c84a07a82a68fe5f83eed9.png)

## _Lightfarm, a multi-award-winning visual arts production house used Marvelous Designer to make ultra-realistic CGI videos. Watch the interesting "Snooze" Project._

* * *

# **Interview with Lightfarm Studios**

* * *

# **1\. Could you briefly introduce your team?**

In 2010, Lightfarm was opened in Auckland, New Zealand. In a short time, the studio gained worldwide notoriety and opened branches in Australia, Singapore, and Brazil, where our largest studio is now located, in Rio de Janeiro. In 2020, Lightfarm opened another new studio in São Paulo, focused mainly on new technologies, specializing in XR (AR and VR). Lightfarm is a multi-award-winning visual arts production house recognized by Cannes and winner of the LIA Grand Prix. Delivering stress-free creative solutions on time and on budget, we build and produce everything, from ultra-realistic CGI images and videos to AR filters and VR applications. Our core values are good service, efficiency, and artistic quality.

# 2\. **Introduction of "Snooze" Project**

"Snooze" is the most ambitious project to date for the Lightfarm teams. To create this 4-minute short film, it was necessary to capture more than 50 scenes in 10 different places over five months of production. To get to the final result, the capture needed to be on triple levels. First, we filmed the dancer in the actual locations, then we filmed the same choreographed take without the dancer, and finally, we re-recorded the choreography of all the scenes to capture movements in our studio. 

With motion capture, our animators were able to bring the virtual character to life. We physically simulated the clothes on an invisible 3D model - a crucial step brilliantly directed by Rafael Coppola using Marvelous Designer. 

** _[Marvelous Designer] Pattern making #1_**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/c48f15b7fa794c85ad72f05ae43e7c24/images/1d2cae0b1ac942c586992f2306cf0c5f1.png)

** _[Marvelous Designer] Pattern making #2_**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/c48f15b7fa794c85ad72f05ae43e7c24/images/6c054ea8f79e4731975514ab73e4549a2.png)

** _[Marvelous Designer] Pattern making #3_**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/c48f15b7fa794c85ad72f05ae43e7c24/images/f0f07ebb612b4da0ac0d36d0b63df8083.png)

** _Final Outfits_**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/c48f15b7fa794c85ad72f05ae43e7c24/images/3f046f51abe5463cbc58e7e3112d9d97%EB%8B%A4%EC%9A%B4%EB%A1%9C%EB%93%9C.png)

To light up the scenes, we capture HDRs from the actual locations and use these HDRs to illuminate the virtual character, thus creating a sense of visual realism. Finally, the post-production, led by Thiago Paladino, composed these different pieces of the puzzle, creating a playful yet realistic composition. 

"Snooze" was a film where we managed to mix all the digital art disciplines in one project for the first time. All of this was possible thanks to high-end software and features, plus an outstanding team of professionals.

**_Video#2 Making Film_**

# **3\. A Brief Workflow in Animation for Snooze Project**

To animate it, Rafael Coppola used an animated model that was the basis of the girl dancing. To try to make the simulation smoother, he simulated with a time step of 60 fps, even though the animation had 30 fps - this means that he simulated the animation with a higher time step than the real animation. He also used a time step of 0.016666666666, and 7 in number of simulation, and also increased gravity a little. The export was all in Alembic with 30 fps, and the thickness was made using C4D. In addition to these softwares, we also used Maya, Houdini, Redshift, Rokoko, Adobe Photoshop, Animate CC, After Effects, Nuke and DaVinci Resolve throughout the project.

# **4\. Would you like to recommend Marvelous Designer to other 3D artists and why?**

"Marvelous Designer is incredible because it offers great editing and creating power of pieces of all levels of complexity. It's fundamental to all my cloth projects", says Coppola.

"Although Marvelous Designer is not made for video, we managed to extract the best from the tool so that it worked beautifully in the film "Snooze", just as we saw in titles like "Love Death and Robots" and "Spiderverse". The clothes simulation and its animation were complex but crucial stages in which Marvelous served us very well to make the main character even more striking!", says Milton Menezes, Director of Snooze.

**_by Lightfarm Studios_**

# **Marvelous Designer Announces USD Support for Integration with NVIDIA Omniverse**

![2e24eb3f2a6d453581d16df07ed6bf09](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/cd5184a887594e258f7232a37fdf7bcb/images/2e24eb3f2a6d453581d16df07ed6bf0945c00f236eb8428dbe855a92d081f238.jpg)

Marvelous Designer has announced at GTC 2021 that we will be releasing USD support for NVIDIA Omniverse this summer.  


USD support is important for any studio looking to the future. As 3D software packages become more complex and divided, it is increasingly difficult to manage workflows and ensure compatibility between lists of programs and their various features. Connecting through USD to Omniverse means pulling many of these stray threads back together, with the goal of making work easier for everyone in the development process.

This connection will allow teams using Marvelous Designer to work together with new levels of cohesion, no matter how they may be separated across offices or time zones. With USD support for Omniverse, your updates become immediately available to the entire group without the need to search emails and chat messages, or navigate cumbersome subversion systems.   


Assets within Omniverse can be viewed and edited, with each modification visible in real time to every connected member. This allows for live collaboration in the same workspace, as though you and the rest of your team are standing over the same table.

**_“NVIDIA has developed a uniquely powerful resource for creators with Omniverse._**

**_With high quality real-time rendering and simulation updates as you work, the building and refining of digital spaces can flow as intuitively as teams of 3D Artists have dreamed it could for decades.”_**

 _by Eric Hinkley, Business Development Manager - Marvelous Designer_

![51abb8e355454dde8589136c9ca1b696](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/cd5184a887594e258f7232a37fdf7bcb/images/51abb8e355454dde8589136c9ca1b69671f517917b8a4e17928745c6d8d29421.jpg)

# **  
Key points for our upcoming integration with NVIDIA Omniverse:**

\- Marvelous Designer will transfer 3D cloth modeling & animation data by USD.

\- Through the built-in USD mechanism, data can be published to the Omniverse Nucleus database (DB) where it can then update all connected digital content creation applications.

\- This mechanism will make it possible to keep track of all local changes since the last publishing event.

\- Marvelous Designer users will be able to simultaneously collaborate with each other by receiving the most currently updated character model and animation files in real time.

\- This development will improve workflows and boost productivity without the hassle of saving files and manually delivering them to your colleagues. 

[**Learn more about NVIDIA Omniverse at GTC**](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/gtc/?ncid=pa-srch-goog-35830#cid=gtcs21_pa-srch-goog_en-us)

# **Interview with Travis Davids | David's Suit | 3D Generalist**

* * *

# **1\. Artist Introduction**

Hello, my name is Travis Davids, I'm from Johannesburg, South Africa and I'm a freelance digital artist and content creator.

I primarily focus on creating 3D related content in the form of tutorials or resources for digital artists.

My content is available on multiple websites like Youtube, Gumroad and Artstation. 

I’m a 3D generalist who loves experimenting with multiple workflows.

I’ve been doing 3D full time since 2015 but my journey started in 2007 when i created mod items for a video game called The Sims.

It sparked my interest to explore an expanding universe of endless possibilities. 

3D gave me a platform to bring my ideas and emotions to life.

It’s something I'm very passionate about and I thoroughly enjoy the endless journey of self improvement. Love what you do and do what you love! 

  


# **2\. What is Marvelous Designer's strong point?**

About 4 years ago I was looking for a really good solution for creating clothing.

Time constraints and having to manually sculpt clothing just wasn’t a viable option for me. 

My only option at the time was sculpting clothing from scratch in ZBrush.

Sculpting every single fold and crease was driving me insane. I have so much respect for artists that can sculpt clothing. 

I searched online and found a solution to my problem in the form of cloth simulation and that program was Marvelous Designer.

It not only allowed me to work faster but the results it generated blew my mind the first time I used it.

The ability to draft a pattern in a 3D program and see it drape on a digital human to generate realistic looking clothing with folds and creases was revolutionary!

At the time, finding learning material online was extremely rare so I had to resort to watching YouTube videos of real fashion designers sewing clothing in order to understand how garments are created.

I still follow this same approach to this day to understand how to draft 2D patterns and sew garments, it has helped me so much.

I feel like the amount of learning material provided for Marvelous Designer today is growing steadily and I made it my duty a couple years ago to record tutorials for Marvelous Designer and put them on YouTube to show everyone how Marvelous Designer could save them so much time to create garments.

I still upload Marvelous Designer tutorials on my channel and I have so much content in development.

Marvelous Designer has become my go to solution for doing anything cloth related. I’ve used it to create a countless number of outfits.

It’s perfect for fashion design but I’ve also used it for environmental props like curtains, bedsheets and pillows. 

Marvelous Designers strong point is speed, customization of garments, accuracy of folds/creases and the ability to iterate and change aspects of a garment with ease, it’s a completely non destructive process and it has become the industry standard. 

# **3\. Artworks created with Marvelous Designer**

**David’s Suit**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/413389959a654ef78910f0e4a1a760f5/images/368ad7da1ed743f489c6b3b7819a9945b6e7fee56bd6487d8b105fd8e12e2808.jpg)

I also reimagined an iconic statue, Michael Angelo’s David and his entire outfit was created with Marvelous Designer. 

**Cyberpunk Bomber Jacket**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/413389959a654ef78910f0e4a1a760f5/images/95f05641169540218782d0ba31469bdd8894fdb375fb4b3b9471c5247f887ae4.jpg)

I created this Cyberpunk Bomber Jacket as an entire course showing you my entire 3D Fashion Design workflow.

You’ll get to see exactly how I build garments like this with Marvelous Designer, ZBrush and Substance Painter on my channel.

I showcase so many useful tools in Marvelous Designer to create the garment.****

**Cyberpunk Leather Jacket**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/413389959a654ef78910f0e4a1a760f5/images/e20e157b964846158059712fc016a50cee5096d0768543bd93f4d02670d57f11.jpg)

This was another Cyberpunk inspired outfit that I created.

I used Marvelous Designer to generate a really good base for me to further detail in ZBrush.

I added detailing to the garment using tileable patterns that I created to generate variations of the design. 

**Rolled Up Fabric**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/413389959a654ef78910f0e4a1a760f5/images/1996d3ffa60a4b57be36cad676e32bad1e6dc36fe32f46f59f20cb643d6109d4.jpg)

Simulating fabric that has been rolled up was very easy to create with Marvelous Designer,

and it helped me achieve the final look for this artwork titled “You Give Me That Feeling”.

title: The Gentleman Fatal
content:
## _INTERVIEW from Winners, 3rd Place in Amateur Category - Hunt: Showdown 3D Apparel Creation Contest. He completes making a hat, shoes and even the ammo belt. Read the whole work in process._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a06327d0be924a10b459c13463cdc533/images/5d7efd6865874531a06f19ecd2a0dbf275e9433679af4651a5c650e437ba4aaf.jpg)

# **By Christian Zollinger-3rd Place in Amateur Category**

* * *

# **1\. Where did you get the inspiration of your hunter?**

The initial and main part of the idea came to me when I looked at the cover of the German version of the graphic novel the airtight garage.

It is written and of course illustrated by the great Jean Giraud / Moebius and the cover depicts the main character, Major Grubert, sitting on a chair in front of a giant dead beast with a shotgun in his hands.

While I looked at the image I remembered the contest and that Hunt Showdown has a distinct lack of " classical safari hunters". Also, the movie Missing link by Laika was still in my head and from there I took the idea that the character might be a posh British adventurer who has kind of seen it all and is on the hunt for new adventures and pray.

So, I started to research who and when exactly this type of clothing was worn and if needed to adjust some things to conform to the time period of hunt.

As it turned out most of the conical stuff like the helmet and the pants, come from British colonial troops from Africa and India and where used from the end of the 19th century till world war 1. Some things like the type of ammo belt that I used as a base are more ww1 onward but I thought it would still fit since some weapons are also ww1 prototypes.

So after a few days of research, I pretty much got the base for my posh Indiana Jones / Safari Hunter type hunter.

# **2\. Could you explain in chronological order what process you went through for the garnet creation of your winning work?**

**1 - Inspiration**

I would start by describing my default process and later explain how I managed to achieve a specific result.

I start most of my projects with an idea I already have in my head.

So my plan for finding an idea is usually to look into Artbooks or comics or sometimes just browse Pinterest and google, till something sparks an idea.

**2 - Research research research**

When I found something I can hook an entire concept on, I start by researching the relevant material. In the case of my hunter, it was primarily looking into British military units of the 19th and early 20th century and very specific into the colonial troops in Africa and India since those were the ones with the iconic helmets. Once I know something about a key item like the helmet I can start to search very specific things like the gear and clothing of these troops. The helmet for example, is the colonial pattern version of the British pith helmet in this case a spiked pith helmet with puggaree and neck curtain.

Since the internet is the internet there are wells of information for anything in my case this website got nearly all the information I needed. [**_(reference﻿)_**](https://http://www.militarysunhelmets.com/2012/a-study-of-the-british-soldier-on-active-service-in-south-africa-1899-1902)

When recreating, the actual name of the garment is very important to achieve authentic results in Marvelous Designer. I found most of the information on the website above. 

I decided to go with a simple button shirt a the pants type called breeches. For the boots I used ankle boots with stonewashed gaiters since it gives off the same silhouette as knee boots but breaks up the surface in interesting ways. The waistcoat was a bigger problem, since I wanted to add the vibe of a hunter to the military uniform. First I thought about leather jerkins with pouches for ammunition shells. but the combination of the jerkins and the breeches accumulated into a very unpleasant silhouette. I went with a leather waistcoat at first but with the introduction of the over shoulder ammunition belt I changed it to a cloth waistcoat without pouches.

The over shoulder belt was introduced relatively late since I wanted to go with a gunslinger style double waist belt but when I searched for different types of belts later on, to get a specific reference I found the "Lee Enfield Leather Bandolier 303" I knew it must be something like this. started looking into over shoulder belts and combined two types of bandoleer with a knife scabbard and a shoulder holster. For the knife, I went with a Kukri to emphasis that he served time in India and has a thing for "exotic or untypical" items.

**3 - sewing patterns**

With all of the parts laid out I researched for sewing patterns that are as close as possible to the parts I wanted to recreate. In the next step I had to test them out, to make sure the fitting and style suits well to my needs. 

Finding the patterns can be a hassle but it is worth it to get an authentic and stylish result. for some parts like the gaiters and the ammo belt, I didn't use a sewing pattern but just a picture of an openly laid out one. Sometimes it is hard to find the right reference and I have to work with what I can get. 

**4 - Building the base garments**

For building the base garments I simply create a square garment and apply a material with a sewing pattern as texture. Then I just trace the pattern with the internal line tool. After that, I place points at all corners and later use the curve tool. I try to keep it as simple as possible at this stage to be able to easily edit the fit when needed. Once I am done with the tracing I just cut out the curve from the pattern and apply a default material with color. I also apply a different color on the inside to be able to distinguish the backside in the 3d view port.

It is important to keep the symmetry on objects as long as possible to make changes easier.

At last I just arrange the parts on the avatar and sew them together.

I repeat this process till I have all the bases ready. Now I can start a first rough fit . This allows me to have an early look at the fit and reiterate the proportions if needed to.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a06327d0be924a10b459c13463cdc533/images/4c2d47d23af946e8ad4881bcfe946d0d691a9bb3eca14a748a34ce389ae973d6.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a06327d0be924a10b459c13463cdc533/images/7e5b093e1a9e435691059d8c50140a814d550a219d084165a41d3ff01260773e.jpg)

**5 - Fitting and adding details**

Next step is to go through the garments one by one and fit them till I'm happy with it. I also qualify them and add details like pockets and roll-up sleeves.

I start to experiment with different physics presets on the material till I find something fitting the look. 

Also, I lower the particle distance to see better how the garment is following and folding.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a06327d0be924a10b459c13463cdc533/images/748dd30bf89641c1a4f2673ac7d614ed%EC%8A%A4%ED%81%AC%EB%A6%B0%EC%83%B7%202025-01-13%20172533.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a06327d0be924a10b459c13463cdc533/images/c0ec11340960451c977339512d4bc5b809aa91a055ec4c719c1145a7ec9488d1.jpg)

**6 - Posing and finalizing the look**

next I posed the avatar and adjusted the draping of some parts so they create a nice looking pose. That is pretty much the standard rundown. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a06327d0be924a10b459c13463cdc533/images/13322ba7740844cab3f47fdcd0095d40fc478cb6a8874164baa94f74414d286c.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a06327d0be924a10b459c13463cdc533/images/7a93ed3143dc4e759ec33f9ca5cd5434868a8bb8991747b5bacda8d100c3829d.jpg)

**7 - Feedback and failure**

long the way, I tried to get feedback very regularly. I send my progress to some friends who are also artist and post them online for example on discord servers or in Facebook groups like 10k/hours.

It is a good sanity check, weather things work like intended and I might get some feedback about things I was not aware of. 

Also, I tried not to get too attached to some ideas. Some things just don't work as intended so I just change them. failure happens to everyone and being perfectionist about an idea that doesn't work that well won't make the piece better. On the waistcoat, for example, I tried different ideas in terms of sewing patterns, placement of bags and strips, till one worked out fine and so I ran with it. Luckily Marvelous makes it very easy to just try out new things :)

Next, I will talk about how I approached specific problems in the creation. 

**The shirt:**

To fold up the sleeves I usually start by adding some internal lines with the offset as a feature. 

I freeze the hole shirt except for the sleeve I am working on.

Now, I give the internal line that I want to fold first a fold angle and a high fold strength. After that, I use pins to get the sleeve to roll up once. When this is done I sew the end of the sleeve to the net internal line.

I repeat that process for the next roll up but I don't sew the last internal line so that the rest of the sleeve still can fold a bit into the rolled-up part.

When I'm done with one sleeve I either do the same thing on the other side or just duplicate the sleeve over to the other side.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a06327d0be924a10b459c13463cdc533/images/4db683e5589842648671e0fbf289f3ea%EC%8A%A4%ED%81%AC%EB%A6%B0%EC%83%B7%202025-01-13%20172735.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a06327d0be924a10b459c13463cdc533/images/6fa77b3f81f643b7b3cc1b9381560605%ED%99%94%EB%A9%B4%20%EC%BA%A1%EC%B2%98%202025-01-13%20172751.png)

In general, I make extensive use of internal lines. 

On the shirt, I used them to create a crease on the top side of the sleeves and to force the topology to work better on the fold on the neckline. Also, I emulate buttons with them. There is a button feature in Marvelous but I don't want to deal with the simulation of the buttons. Often I find it easier to just add them later.

I play around with seam taping quite a bit, on the shirt I used it to give the collar more stiffness and prevent it from folding too much on the outer edges. For the collar I like to use a bit stiffer material. The shirt was primarily simulated with the linen preset, the collar with denim. Also, I simulated the shirt one more time at the end with the Mysoftest material from Rosemary, to give the folds a more saggy and the shirt overall a more worn out look. [**_(reference)_**](https://www.deviantart.com/rosemaryr94901/art/MD5-Presets-for-version-2-3-153-and-up-592231722)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a06327d0be924a10b459c13463cdc533/images/67be44b6f54846b39e67f506849642fe%EC%8A%A4%ED%81%AC%EB%A6%B0%EC%83%B7%202025-01-13%20172843.png)

For double layers like on the pants, I plot out the part that I need to be doubled with an internal line on the first layer. When I'm happy with the shape I copy the layer on top, cut the internal line and delete the parts that I don't need. Then I just need to sew the layers together, freeze the first layer and hit simulate. Once the second layer is simulated I get everything back to layer 0.

I also use the pressure and shrinkage on the garments to control their behavior. I used pressure on the holster with a very minimal amount just so that it does not float too much away from the body. The boots have a slide amount of shrinkage to ensure that they don't sag and the gaiters got some pressure to make them stay where they are supposed to be.

I often use pressure for shirts that need to be tucked in. Since sometimes the simulation has problems with stuff that is very near to the body and has layers on top of it, I try to get the shirt as close to the body as possible without a big fold so that it simulates nicely under the pants.

For this to happen I just freeze the collar and sleeves and then apply negative pressure to the shirt so that it will be sucked on the body. now I activate the pants and freeze them two. Next I get the pressure back to 0 and hit simulate. Once the shirt is extended again I stop the simulation and unfreeze the pants. Now, I simulate again and that's it.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a06327d0be924a10b459c13463cdc533/images/a95ef04d852546368599a903668992ea%EC%8A%A4%ED%81%AC%EB%A6%B0%EC%83%B7%202025-01-13%20172916.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a06327d0be924a10b459c13463cdc533/images/c6205bb889ad42bda3b88369f4c4da86%ED%99%94%EB%A9%B4%20%EC%BA%A1%EC%B2%98%202025-01-13%20172931.png)

To ensure the straps on the gaiters do not slide down I heightened the friction of the material on the gaiters. this way it was easier to control how much they slide and also manipulate it. After I was satisfied with their position I applied some pressure again to make them stay.

One very Interesting part to figure out how to build the soles of the boots. Since there is no way I know of to build hard surface objects in Marvelous he problem was to connect the sewing pattern of the boots with the avatar object, since the sole determines the lower part of the silhouette of the boots.

After some fiddling around I finally realized that meshes can be imported as garment and the UV maps can be used as the pattern. This way I could create a nice workaround. At first I modeled the soles in Blender and UV'ed them. I layed out the UV? islands on top, so that the inserted part would be its own island. The sole had to stick out from the boot a bit. Importing the soles to Marvelous as garment and used the UV as a pattern. Now,the soles were in and had patterns to interact with. Since I gave the inset of the soles it’s own UV island I could now sew the rest of the boot onto it. I just needed to keep the soles frozen all the time. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a06327d0be924a10b459c13463cdc533/images/a9baa432328b46eb9b84f3ae9c617ad3%EC%8A%A4%ED%81%AC%EB%A6%B0%EC%83%B7%202025-01-13%20173018.png)

Importing a mesh as pattern made the creation of the hat very easy. I just had to pre build a model of the helmet in Blender and cut the UV the same way I would lay out the sewing pattern. After that, I imported the mesh as a garment. The base was ready. I just needed to do some cleanup on some points and the sewing. I took a slightly deflated version of the helmet as an avatar, this way I could just simulate the pattern without problems. With the shrinkage and pressure values, I had control over the shape and very quickly went into creating the puggaree.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a06327d0be924a10b459c13463cdc533/images/ad20ba28f7b140d9b186bb156a1e95929760820da2da4d6fb42391fdff9387f1.jpg)

The ammunition belt was pretty much just a lot of offset as an internal line and split line.

I started by figuring out how much pockets I wanted and if the measurement for the pockets checks out.

After I found my measurements I just started adding internal lines and splitting them. making sure the lines had enough curve points so the split won't deform them.

From here on it was just a lot of placing points and lines. I wish there were a feature to do the same split line operation on multiple lines at once.

After I got the layout, I built the straps for the first pocket and sewed it on. It worked very well, so I duplicated it, but welded them later to keep everything changeable..

This is pretty much everything I did in Marvelous.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a06327d0be924a10b459c13463cdc533/images/2bafbed2037e40f78e37790618d64009add6e296d26c4dde9385229f5a0feff7.jpg)

I imported everything to Blender and arranged the UV layout. It just needed to be workable, so I did pretty fast and tidy. Mainly I separated the lower and upper body as well as the props into their low texture sets. Also fixed some minor things like floating rivets. 

I also baked the high poly onto the high poly to get some maps like curvature and position as information for the texturing process.

next up is Substance Painter. 

I started by giving everything a base material from the material library to get a feeling for the textures.

After that, I experimented a lot with the materials and different generators to get some nice dirt and sun bleaching.

Since there was no ZBrush pass for this project I added memory folds in Substance Painter. For an overall effect, I combined a generator map from Substance with a wrinkle alpha to get some folds on the whole object, then I painted in memory folds at the seams with seam alphas.

Also I added a slight gradient to the diffuse textures to slightly emphasis the upper half of the hunter.

During the texturing process I exported the textures to CryEngine to be able to see, how they appear in the final scene. It appears quite different. For example the normal information from the memory folds, were way more visible in CryEngine, then in Substance Painter. I needed to scale those back quite a bit.

Also, the colors turned out slightly different. It might have something to do with the render engines in general but also the lighting is very different in the hunt scene. I chose the CryEngine hunt scene for the final render because it gives off a very distinctive hunt vibe. I am not deep enough into the whole render game to set up scene of equal quality, plus I could just position my hunter inside the scene with the other hunters and match it

# **3\. What was the most difficult part, and what part did you spend a lot of time on to complete this artwork?**

I think the hardest part is to translate the idea in my head into an actual garment. Getting the fit and feel of the garments right is very important to make believable 3D drapery . Also working it into an interesting silhouette is a part I still struggle with.

From a crafting a spekt attaching the patterns of the boots to a sole and solving the helmet has been the hardest part to figure out. In the end, I could use the same approach for both problems.

The part where I spent the most time on was the ammo belt.

Figuring out the patterns and measurements already took long enough. But to get it to simulate correctly with all the attachments was quite a piece of work.

# **4\. What are the strong points that Marvelous Designer has?**

The biggest strong point for me is the fast simulation and editing process, which enables me to think spontaneously and in the flow. Marvelous lets me try out variations very quick and easy, so I can make better decisions on what ideas I want to take further and always go back if needed. 

For me Marvelous Designer is kind of like a swiss knife for 3D clothing. It let me translate real world sewing patterns into 3D meshes without much of a hassle. On top Marvelous delivers a high level of realism that would be hard to craft by hand, but doesn’t restrict you to being realistic. It is a big deal for me to be able to express authentic clothing when making 3D models for games. And the fact that Marvelous lets you visualize your ideas in such a n easy and fluid way makes it a tool that I really like working with.

Also being able to import UV’ed meshes as a garment with a sewing pattern proved to be a tremendous help. This way you can import very specific shapes and especially hard surface stuff, but still be able to interact with them, like I did with the soles of the boots.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a06327d0be924a10b459c13463cdc533/images/2b4b087122684b7c9cb2bbaf30462abb1bd315ea870d49909ffe5a10173d1830.jpg)

**_By Christian Zollinger_**

## _INTERVIEW from Winners, 2nd Place in Amateur Category - Hunt: Showdown 3D Apparel Creation Contest._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a5a198322a924793a7a827cddcd4f1fe/images/51e65cf892d04e6da515f64d8984d6c30ee512a5e8874bd6ac85b8c702f84ecd.jpg)

# **By Ana Zlatkovic - 2nd Place in Amateur Category**

* * *

# **1\. Where did you get the inspiration of your hunter?**

A few months prior to the contest, I had access to a book with beautiful illustrations of the Victorian era fashion depicting lavish dresses of this era. When the contest started, I remembered all those crinolines, corsets, folds and ruffles, and I knew I wanted Victorian elements in my design. With that in mind, I started my research mainly relying on online resources. **  
**

# **2\. Could you explain in chronological order what process you went through for the garment creation of your winning work?**

I first focused on general research of the Victorian era. My first goal was to learn as much as possible about life in the 19th century, not just the way people dressed, but also what their everyday activities were, how social structure affected their activities and how it defined fashion characteristics of that time. 

Then I compiled a collection of reference photos to help me organize and remember all the specific Victorian fashion details.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a5a198322a924793a7a827cddcd4f1fe/images/6c01a50299a84f758236249ed3369fa250ff363b2c3c49e1a13e3467bdba9e0d.jpg)

Victorian dresses had multiple layers and a lot of lacy, ruffled details, especially the dresses worn by the upper class members. That is why at this point I needed to decide what fashion elements my garments should include. 

The next step was to find a way to simplify and modernize the design to make it practical. I always kept in mind the fact that my outfit was meant for a hunter who should be able to move easily, to hunt efficiently. That is why I chose to leave out crinoline, long train and heavy draping. 

I printed out some of the reference photos and created a collage to help me see what kind of clothing pieces can be nicely combined. 

Then I started testing potential parts of my design in Marvelous Designer. I created a few variations of each garment (a blouse with more ruffles, a blouse with less ruffles, wider pants, narrow leg pants, a couple of collar options...) and I started dressing the mannequin and combining different variations of my garments. This is how I filtered garment variations that I liked the most.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a5a198322a924793a7a827cddcd4f1fe/images/3314c63ff95e48119cf7fb728f90ffb68724ca312e844e8b84088ce356e279c5.jpg)

My final design was the product of the elimination process followed by some additional detailing and polishing. 

# **3\. What was the most difficult part, and what part did you spend a lot of time on to complete this artwork?**

Intricate and luxurious Victorian dresses are pretty and fascinating, but I thought that a clean and simple design was more suitable for a hunter. Deciding which fashion details specific to the Victorian era to exclude from my final design was the most difficult part of the process.

In terms of actual creation of the design, the most difficult and the most time consuming part was to make certain stubborn parts of my garments to simulate properly. 

For example, the blouse I made had many small pleats, and all that fabric bunched up in contact with the corset, which made the simulation more difficult. 

It required patience and a lot of careful tweaking to get it right. Layering settings and particle distance adjustments definitely helped with that.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a5a198322a924793a7a827cddcd4f1fe/images/8bb733ecec71412b9d248db23ceb4c139d42ae30c8c74112b40fc6ce12468f3d.png)

The corset train, which had two layers and a pleat along the center back line, also required a few attempts to simulate well.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a5a198322a924793a7a827cddcd4f1fe/images/221c6d1b160d4001b5a6c530ce6e478381647f84e5b44cffbe3886715c0fca1f.png)

# **4\. What are the strong points that Marvelous Designer has?**

Marvelous Designer enables easy and fast design testing. Even when I am working with a pattern that is not completely accurate, fast simulation shows me right away whether I am on the right track, and I can quickly spot the parts of the design I want to improve or eliminate.

Also, thanks to its numerous functionalities and settings it is possible to achieve a very detailed result without help from any other software.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a5a198322a924793a7a827cddcd4f1fe/images/f554c7224d484c2da91ecc03f1f35da467827f09e3074b39bb35138cad3961f7.jpg)

_Thanks for the interview and your amazing work, Ana Zlatkovic!_

## _Travis Davids shares a breakdown of how South Parks iconic character, Kenny’s outfit was created, with a big, medium, small approach with the garments._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/0e13aa14ba6647138b84c7e5932bf5df/images/e1a6165933bb46c18d0157ad6c77c11ee8da6fea12c74b85bfdef7b7fb81e6c1.png)

# **Interview with Travis Davids| South Park | 3D Generalist**

* * *

# **1\. Artist Introduction**

Hello, my name is Travis Davids, I'm from Johannesburg, South Africa and I'm a freelance digital artist and content creator.

I primarily focus on creating 3D related content in the form of tutorials or resources for digital artists. My content is available on multiple websites like YouTube, Gumroad and Artstation.

I’m a 3D generalist who loves experimenting with multiple workflows.

I’ve been doing 3D full time since 2015 but my journey started in 2007 when i created mod items for a video game called The Sims. It sparked my interest to explore an expanding universe of endless possibilities.

3D gave me a platform to bring my ideas and emotions to life. It’s something I'm very passionate about and I thoroughly enjoy the endless journey of self improvement.

Love what you do and do what you love!

# **2\. Workflow for your artworks with a brief introduction**

I used Marvelous Designer to create realistic outfits for all of my reimagined characters for South Park.

**Reimagining South Park Characters**

I followed the same approach for every garment. I will do a breakdown of how Kenny’s outfit was created. 

All of my garments start with the most basic building blocks. I follow a Big, Medium, Small approach with my garments. 

**Big** Basic shapes and buildings blocks to create a basic template with a great fit. 

**Medium** Detailing the garment, adding new elements to the design.

**Small** Adding smaller details like internal lines for topstitching, seams, buttons, and layer clones as well as reducing the particle distance to 5 or 3.

Detailing the garment further in Zbrush and bringing it to completion is also included during this phase. 

**Creating The Base (BIG)**

I focus primarily on creating a garment with a good base.

Once you have a good base created that fits your avatar correctly, you can transform that basic template into a variety of different garments.

In this case, I had a long sleeve t-shirt I created that fit Kenny perfectly and I tweaked it to turn it into a jacket.

This saved me some time from having to create the base garment from scratch. 

I use Daz Studio to generate my human characters. They are fully rigged and easy to pose. 

I always create my garments on a character that is in a T-Pose or A-Pose.

It makes your life a lot easier to create the patterns and drape a garment on a symmetrical pose.

Later on once you’re detailing the garment further you can transition to a different pose.

I also keep my particle distance on 20 or 15 during the early stages for the sake of performance.

I’ll also use GPU simulation in certain instances to see my simulation results in what can only be described as real time and then go back to normal simulation mode for accurate results.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/0e13aa14ba6647138b84c7e5932bf5df/images/86da97e0bfb243c29a3cd56dd6e7f2d13f4a510bfd90475c952333479055757a.png)

**QUICK TIP:** When you are creating your basic shapes, don’t add curvature to the pattern while you’re drafting it, add this afterwards by using the “Edit Curvature” tool.

You will thank yourself later because by adding curvature afterwards, if you go to “Edit Pattern” you will have access to anchor points that you can adjust to control the amount of curvature.

This makes the process of adjusting curvature non destructive and easy to change. 

**Transitioning To A Different Pose**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/0e13aa14ba6647138b84c7e5932bf5df/images/f14a43b058594ff9a94d951d20405100cfb72430c3f14fb1a395b0030f6c3fb9.jpg)

Once I have a good base I'll actually use morph targets to see how my garment looks in a different pose.

Since I’m using morph targets i can easily go back to the a-pose if I need to further adjust my garment. 

QUICK TIP: There are various ways to transition to different poses but an easy method is to use morph targets.

If you saved out two obj’s of your character (a-pose and posed), import the a-pose first and drape your garment on the a-pose.

Now go to “File” “Import OBJ” and instead of importing an OBJ as an avatar, import it as a morph target so change “Object Type” to Morph Target.

Your character will transition from the a-pose to the next pose. 

**Detailing The Garment Further (MEDIUM)**

During this phase I decrease my particle distance to 10 just to see a better representation of my fabric.

Since the garment is going to be getting more detailed I might lose some performance but i can always go back to 15.

The majority of my time is spent on this process by creating new garment pieces like the hood, adjusting fabric settings, choosing different fabric colors,

adding render thickness to the garment to get a much better idea of what the garment looks like with thickness and changing it to “Thick Textured Surface” to see the end result.

I always add thickness in Marvelous Designer even if i plan on exporting a thin version of the garment.

If I'm going to add thickness in zbrush, I can just reference the thickness I created in MD.

Garments are usually not paper thin and by adding just a subtle layer of thickness, it gives the garment a much better visual representation. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/0e13aa14ba6647138b84c7e5932bf5df/images/b38163beadd44cdb826cef12f0fc8a1f37296d5c5c314d63b85244254e20b19a.png)

**QUICK TIP** : Use Marvelous Designer 10’s brand new “Quality Render” feature to see what a garment looks like with ambient occluded shadows.

It gives you a much better representation of what the garment would look like if I was actually rendered. Folds and wrinkles look so much better with this enabled. 

**Adding The Finer Details (SMALL)**

Now it’s all about the small details. Since I was creating a jacket and I wanted it to visually look warmer, I created a layer clone of the garment.

A layer clone doubles up your fabric and is a fantastic method to make garments look thicker/warmer.

Any internal lines that you have included on your pattern will be a lot more visible on a layer clone.

It’s almost like adding the icing on top of a cake and works very well if you’re creating jackets.

Keep in mind that sometimes you might need to change the layer order of a layer clone to prevent it from causing simulation issues,

and then bring it back to its original number to make everything simulate correctly.

I add internal lines along the seams of the garment and adjust the fold angle to make them more predominant. 

Once i’m happy, i’ll reduce my particle distance to 5 or 3 to get the best quality possible.

I’ll also quandragulate my garment in MD if i plan on taking it over to zbrush for additional sculpting. I’ll also arrange my UV’s in MD’s UV Editor so everything is nice and organized. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/0e13aa14ba6647138b84c7e5932bf5df/images/39fa1144851d44f68d701b0ad64ee2bdc8344b97d4dc41f0b4a43d89b369c398.png)

Since I didn't intend on adding thickness in another program to this garment,

I could select my entire pattern for different garment pieces, go to “File” “Export OBJ Selected” and export my garment as “Multiple Objects", "Thick”,

and I make sure “Unified UV Coordinates” is selected. I also put my scale on “cm (Daz Studio) and my % at 100% and then click on ok. 

QUICK TIP: If you’ve created a garment with multiple pieces like a t-shirt, jacket and pants, export these pieces individually instead as one garment.

It keeps everything organized to have these garments separated as their own OBJ’s. 

  


**Assembling The Scene**

For Kenny’s outfit I only did a little bit of detailing in Zbrush by sculpting additional folds but Marvelous Designer did all of the heavy lifting.

I assemble my scenes in Cinema 4D and create all of my materials with Octane Render.

With certain garments I'll also do my texturing in Substance Painter or create my own tileable materials from scratch with Substance Designer.

The scene is basic with only 2 area lights. I also used the power of artificial intelligence from Artbreeder to generate a realistic human face for Kenny.

If you want to see my entire workflow I have uploaded a breakdown video on youtube via [this link.](https://youtu.be/AClov4mK-PU)
