## _Morten Jaeger reveals his process of creating artwork, from conceptualization to final texturing._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/315e3674b22042cdbc5299b90afc1f68/images/b1fa16adb0714a4d8e59fb5a4a4de1726027340f19684c8cbc96afa6ff4aa227.jpg)

# **Interview with Morten Jaeger| MS. MARVELOUS |**

# **Co-Founders of FlippedNormals**

* * *

# **1\. Introduction**

My name is Morten and I’m one of the Co-Founders of FlippedNormals. Flippednormals is a digital marketplace that curates digital assets and tutorials.

We strive for quality, and as a result, only provide our customers with the highest quality CG products on the market. Before starting our marketplace I worked in VFX where I had the opportunity to work in such films as Pacific Rim: Uprising, Guardians Of The Galaxy Vol. 2, Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald and many more. There’s been a bit of a vacuum when it comes to Marvelous Designer training lately and having used it on multiple blockbusters throughout my career, I felt I could bring some valuable knowledge to the table.**  
**

# **2\. Inspiration**

As with any project, I always go on a reference hunt. One thing that stood out to me was the style of clothing. Seeing as I wanted to create a costume for a woman, I noticed a trend of baggy pants with a crop top most of the time.

I wanted to spice it up a bit, so I decided to add a sports bra along with the tied sweater. I was very inspired by the K/DA - POP/STARS music video from Riot, as well as various hip hop dancers on Instagram. With that in mind, I wanted to create something appealing—not just in terms of clothing but also as a polished portfolio piece.

What they did in terms of the color palette for the K/DA music video was a big inspiration. I went through many different iterations before settling on the final colors. Though the color of the costume was established fairly early on, these came from my reference "I.AM.GIA Pants".

I did several attempts to get the look of these pants just right, and they ended up dictating the palette for the rest of the costume.  


# **3\. Creating the garment**

I always start out very basic. No curves, no elaborate shapes.

This is the same approach I have whether I’m painting, sculpting, or making fabrics. It’s a lot easier to tweak your design before you add lots of detail and become too attached to your design. So I can’t stress the importance of this enough.

That, combined with the first step—collecting good references—will improve your designs and save you time in the long run.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/315e3674b22042cdbc5299b90afc1f68/images/0d19624d4edc4ab5b2ba5e2d79a6bb1cca168f5f1b924a0986dc15b09462fde6.jpg)

Throughout the process, I make great use of temporary pins. These allow me to suspend things in mid-air or on the model, with the benefit that I can easily clear them if I no longer need them.

It’s very similar to creating garments in real life. You won’t always have perfect measurements from the beginning, so having pins you can quickly add and remove really speeds up my workflow.

I try to stay basic until I have all areas of the garment nailed down, but I never focus too heavily on one area. This allows me to better evaluate the state of the costume, ensuring that no one part is too detailed compared to the rest.  


I also believe that a good base mesh can do wonders for your costumes. It’s like having a good model to pose with your brand.

For this tutorial, I used a base mesh provided by Vail Peychev, who makes some amazing base meshes. The pose fit really well with what I was going for, and it helps set the stage for the mood of the piece as well.

There’s something about having a semi-posed model to show off your garments—it just makes it come more alive.

This obviously wouldn’t work if I was working on a production piece, as the pose isn’t very rigging-friendly. But in this instance, that didn’t really matter.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/315e3674b22042cdbc5299b90afc1f68/images/f243f2abdc2f46ec96de92486b9f0b68aea7b6603b05424cb0843c37cee27e63.jpg)

# **4\. The Secret to Details**

One of the best ways I know to add detail is by using internal lines. Internal lines with varying fold strengths can create the feel of seams and depressions in your fabric.

This is the very last step of my garment creation process, as by this point, you shouldn’t really change anything design-wise.

For thicker garments like the top sweater, I increased the fold strength significantly to give the impression of a heavier, thicker garment.

On the other hand, for the pants, I did the opposite. These were intended to be made of lightweight nylon, a very thin and light fabric.

In that case, it wouldn’t make sense to create too deep of a depression, as it would make the material appear thicker than it should be.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/315e3674b22042cdbc5299b90afc1f68/images/d0111658df434c939cfbc5e7b284f801bf0a134180a442a5a1923d1a45532fc5.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/315e3674b22042cdbc5299b90afc1f68/images/d4b342f901c2459b944a7448c9a80f4f7214c84d5e014c4c8f0b8e094474d1ac.jpg)

# **5\. Tying the Knot**

By far, the hardest part was tying the sweater around her waist. It wasn’t something I had seen done before, so I had to get creative to solve it.

Marvelous Designer is excellent at detecting surfaces and generally seems to understand what you want the fabric to do. However, things get a bit different when you compress and stretch the fabric a lot.

I used a combination of a really low **Particle Distance** to achieve a more accurate simulation and tweaked various friction parameters to ensure the fabric clung to itself.

The biggest challenge here was making Marvelous understand that I wanted the garment to twist, without allowing it to resolve into its default relaxed state.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/315e3674b22042cdbc5299b90afc1f68/images/9566ce95a1124efc88d909d3f23340ff7a854e36066c4f2db03b1355abf1da39.jpg)

Using temporary pins, I pulled the sleeves of the sweater apart to tie it. Once I had a shape I was satisfied with, I adjusted the friction parameters to make it stay in place.

Otherwise, you run into the issue where Marvelous starts creating intersections, and your garment ends up looking like the beginnings of a black hole.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/315e3674b22042cdbc5299b90afc1f68/images/28acadc3d3734bd98c823db00d127899e800ea69d90c46629e564594c8ed9a12.jpg)

# **6\. Painting with Substance**

Before this project, I had never really used Substance Painter that much. So it was a perfect opportunity for me to get properly into the software.

Texturing was never really a big passion of mine, but after finishing this project and working with Painter, I’m a lot more excited about it. 

The textures were kept pretty simple, mostly using fill layers to keep it as procedural as possible.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/315e3674b22042cdbc5299b90afc1f68/images/448787fa8ce34d4d83cbdea32dfc8eb583054cfa8c3b4705942c823033e4a61b.jpg)

The only time I really used regular paint layers, were for the emissive masks and the makeup on the face.

The great thing about Painter is that I could upscale the resolution if I needed to. So I started fairly low-res with the procedural layers just to make my life easier. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/315e3674b22042cdbc5299b90afc1f68/images/e1a563deb8e543acb981b6e6a3a252003ec58a7b3c354fdebd7dd20521325b96.jpg)

**7\. Finishing Touches** ﻿

For the final resolution, I set the particle distance to 3 for most objects. This was a bit heavy, but I needed the ultrafine details that Marvelous creates.

To finish everything off, I imported my completed garment into ZBrush and applied **FlippedNormals Fabrics** to add an extra layer of realism. This is exactly what they were designed for, and by combining them with **NoiseMaker** inside ZBrush, you can achieve some pretty cool results.

The default fabrics are quite clean, but that has the added benefit of making it easier to introduce imperfections and aging effects.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/315e3674b22042cdbc5299b90afc1f68/images/5e2fefb7685643c690da3bc428c040b221776dac44d049109108b24841afb1fd.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/315e3674b22042cdbc5299b90afc1f68/images/481e31cc199a4e329ee752bfbe094c601a7c54a59217415aaca275a7decc366a.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/315e3674b22042cdbc5299b90afc1f68/images/af203c2a2cdd477899da7c212fd5c5ccdeb43b4aedea41249fb09eb5f8443a90.jpg)

**_by Morten Jaeger – Co-Founders of FlippedNormals  
_**

## _INTERVIEW from Winners, the 1st Place in Professional Category - Hunt: Showdown 3D Apparel Creation Contest_

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/303925096cd54ce58ec60e2f876bd3e6/images/a1d25a6feff641e58b990db198a2207b92dafd8388c24d6f808048eb5a3b8ab8.jpg)

# **By Andrzej Rać-1st Place in Professional Category**

* * *

# **Where did you get the inspiration of your hunter?**

The inspiration for me was the actual game. I've tried to find all of the hunters that were in the game.

Luckily, I have the power of the internet at my disposal so it's super easy to do.

This allowed me to break all characters into parts, compare them, look at what they have in common and what the differences are, and finally what I would like to see in game and it wasn't there.

Then I have spent a considerable amount of time on Pinterest. I was browsing all sorts of clothing pictures from the time period and saved everything that caught my eye.

I think at this point I've decided to do a huntress and not a hunter. I find that women's clothing is usually far more interesting and fun to recreate.

After that I simply looked through everything I had and did a selection of what to throw away and finished with a few reference pictures to work with.

I was trying to go for something that she could wear when going for example to the city.

I imagined it would be a bit nicer and decorative but still suitable to work around the house everyday.

Loose shirt detailed around the neck and high waist pants loose around thighs, held together by leather wraps around the shins.

I've also added a leather loop to the belt and an axe for the times when You run out of ammo, and little red piece of cloth around the neck.

Looking at my design now I can see that I really didn't go that far away from the in-game designs.

I just mixed all the parts that I liked the most in different hunters.

I took a long coat, cowboy like hat and shoulder holsters and put them on the clothing I've found on Pinterest.

# **Could you explain in chronological order what process you went through for the garment creation of your winning work?**

First and the most important thing for me after gathering my reference pictures was to find good sewing patterns,

because no matter how good Marvelous Designer is (and it's simply marvelous),

to simulate good looking garments, You have to create them the proper way.

Just like in real life where we have the best physical simulations, clothes won't look good if they were made the wrong way.

For the shirt, pants and the coat I started with Pants and T-shirt garments from Marvelous Garment Library.

Because there is no point to start from scratch.

I then modified those patterns to achieve desired look and assigned different materials to all parts to get different colors and appropriate physical properties.

For gloves I traced patterns from photo texture. I created a plane and assigned texture to its material and then edited the 2d texture to fill the plane.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/303925096cd54ce58ec60e2f876bd3e6/images/57d71b765309463397c977103bc8f58b%EC%8A%A4%ED%81%AC%EB%A6%B0%EC%83%B7%202024-01-21%20210046.png)

From here you simply trace what you see on the texture with the "Internal Polygon/Line" tool under the "G" key.

After you are done, you can select created edges, right click them and "CUT" out of the plane.

I did that to all the parts and sew them together on my character. ﻿

I think the hat and the cloth on the neck are the only things i did by hand and figured out how the patterns could look like without reference, because their shapes are simple enough to do that.

I keep different garments on different layers so there is no problem with overlapping when I simulate them.

For example, shirt is on layer 0 and pants on layer 1,Marvelous Designer automatically treats the shirt as tucked in because it is on the lower layer. It is very useful functionality.

Most patterns had Particle Distance set to 15mm. This setting was a good balance between optimal mesh density and simulation results.

I kept this until everything was in place and all parts of the garment had nice volume and shape.

From here I added buttons and seam taping in places where usually clothes are being sewed together (sleeve connection to body, front and back part connection and outside borders).

Seam taping reinforces those edges and makes the whole garment look more realistic. At least that's how I understand it's functionality.

With everything in place it was time to pose my character.

Until this moment, i worked with a simple mannequin shared by the Hunt Showdown team but it had no skeletal.

So i could not use it anymore. I have imported the Female Hunter model into Blender, posed it and key framed everything, then exported the final mesh with its animation into FBX file.

After switching avatars, you can go from Simulation to Animation tab. And, simply play your animation, and your avatar will change it's pose.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/303925096cd54ce58ec60e2f876bd3e6/images/9f0efe67bf02435b94a898ba8fe3e5db%EC%8A%A4%ED%81%AC%EB%A6%B0%EC%83%B7%202024-01-21%20210244.png)

The process of posing garments was pretty straight forward. Freezing everything except pants and animating them to a new pose,

then freezing pants, going back to frame 0, unfreezing shirt and animating it to a new pose and so on.

I did this until everything was in it's final place. This took some time but animating everything at once was way

beyond capabilities of my machine and I had to manage somehow.

Now it was time to get my final meshes with proper density and best looking simulations.

Like with animating, i worked with one piece at a time. I changed the particle distance to 5mm to get nice folds.

I set Shrinkage weft and warp values to over 100% to "get more cloth" inside a single pattern without need to scale anything.

I found this useful trick in one of the tutorials on YouTube.

Then I changed mesh type from triangle to "Quad" and finally in simulation property I switched preset from Normal to "Complete (Nonlinear)" simulation type.

It is much heavier to compute for your PC but gives better looking results.

After all that you can simply export everything to OBJ files.

Marvelous Designer can automatically add thickness to your garment and include all the buttons you create.

For this kind of work it's extremely helpful because it saves time.

From here I worked on my UV's in Blender and Textures in Substance Painter and that's it.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/303925096cd54ce58ec60e2f876bd3e6/images/6ac70455907045d588c91bc88a3d1ee35046926e376b4692bdc0ad4377d3a2a3.jpg)

# **What was the most difficult part, and what part did you spend a lot of time on to complete this artwork?**

The Biggest headache was the posing of the coat and it was the most difficult part for me.

Firstly because it lays on top of everything and in basic position it is strongly intersected with other parts that are already in final place.

Secondly it's being pushed to the back by hands and it wasn't folding the way I wanted.

For this I had to use the Pin tool. It helped me to move it and hold the coat in certain positions during simulation which allowed me to avoid errors while animating.

I still had to move my pins to a new position every one or two frames but it did the work.

There's probably a better way to do this, but I had no time to experiment with different solutions.

Animating I think was the part that I spent most time on. Mostly because I never did it before.

# **What are the strong points that Marvelous Designer has?**

One of the strongest points of Marvelous Designer is the fact that it can run even on slower machines.

You can always change particle distance to higher values and speed things up this way.

\- Thanks to real fabric presets You will always achieve realistic effects.

There is no guesswork if something looks off, You know that is Your fault and there's something wrong with the way You created Your patterns.

\- New manual retopology tool is also amazing.

It's super easy to draw quads in 2D View. You instantly see how everything lays out in 3d and can create low res versions of garments for other softwares to reproject the high detail.

I think those three are my absolute favorites but I am still learning this software so who knows what else I will find in the future.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/303925096cd54ce58ec60e2f876bd3e6/images/0ad263e3a23647fa9bb0c7fa6b1709832eb66075f3f84c4d81f0d1c777c3afaf.jpg)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/303925096cd54ce58ec60e2f876bd3e6/images/c6320bfb105f412d92f9df05a8f38c25de95d94203354d20bc9530ad8042bcbe.jpg)

_Link to_[** _Artstation_**](https://www.artstation.com/andrzej_rac)

title: THE SHIKARI (THE HUNTER)
content:
## **_INTERVIEW from Winners | Hunt: Showdown 3D Apparel Creation Contest_**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a404fc144f9e461c8f933e8ce0625a12/images/123debb8598c4587b879c54fa2912795085514a651424f619e0e6dfa3abe755f.png)

# **By Shaafi Ahamd -1st Place in Amateur Category**

* * *

# **Where did you get the inspiration of your hunter?**

When I decided to take part in the contest, I had a couple ideas in mind of hunters from different parts of the world, but I settled on one from the Indian subcontinent.

It’s something which hasn’t been done much and I believed I could make something really unique with that idea and my own design choices.

My reference board had images of Mughal and British-era soldiers, princes, Cossacks, along with Turkic warriors.

Making it equipped for fighting while maintaining the local look and also balancing the overall design was a challenge.

# **Could you explain in chronological order what process you went through for the garment creation of your winning work?**

I started the outfit off with the shoes and boots. Making any type of footwear in Marvelous Designer was an unknown and I wanted to tackle that first.

One thing I learned was that changing the material type and its various properties is crucial to getting any decent result.

There are a large amount of presets and “Trim_Full_Grain_Leather” is great for anything hard and stiff like the sole of a shoe.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a404fc144f9e461c8f933e8ce0625a12/images/741d5821e3eb420e8b514ec51aab7736708ba0424b08424c9c6efc37c27ef5fe.jpg)

I found that pulling and pinning to control and mold the garments is essential.

Getting garments within one another or looping them through each other is done this way.

Cloth pieces can also be held in place with pins to stop them from sliding around and ruining the look.

I made the waist wrap by putting many pattern strips into position with arrangement points and then just wrapped them round and round.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a404fc144f9e461c8f933e8ce0625a12/images/4ccb1ec9bd004cf78b45621d2b728c53658c3caf83b142f3b55a1f1585598102.jpg)

The same was done with the turban but this was more tricky. The cloth pieces slid and a combination of pinning and un-pinning was required so it could look natural.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a404fc144f9e461c8f933e8ce0625a12/images/a6455219e43f416bb68ffab64738f9a8c246f3ae08774af289471b2cefed125f.jpg)

After getting the general shape of the pants I used the Shrinkage Weft and Warp options to get the baggy look and folds. 

This way you can experiment a ton without even touching the actual pattern.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a404fc144f9e461c8f933e8ce0625a12/images/848bd940f3344625bd4dba5430590d5827b1d22bfdec4039bbd1e589ca339344.jpg)

Making the tassels was a simple but laborious process of free-sewing a ton of pattern strips. Since there was an overlap of various garments, using the layers option resolved some simulation issues.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a404fc144f9e461c8f933e8ce0625a12/images/897f09924a214cd9a2d045beb8c3e4bb94265493ccc54e87a7109bb018624d2e.jpg)

I incorporated a lot of internal lines in the shirt to add some visual interest. Mixing different

materials, like I did here with cotton and leather straps, can result in interesting results. For the backside of the bandolier I did the following: 1) Made one single, long pattern. 2) Added a single internal line at an angle. 3) While duplicating the line with CTRL C & V, I right clicked to set the number of lines and interval distance. 4) I then cut and sewed to get pieces and changed the material.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a404fc144f9e461c8f933e8ce0625a12/images/98ad5a5ac8024e328d346de88b91bba909fb19648da04339b908aa97ac898cde.jpg)

The symbols in each pocket are just internal lines with thicker top-stitching.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a404fc144f9e461c8f933e8ce0625a12/images/7e49f49ecc6c42cea7468dff66b33e39ba1963d7fa044a1da610b21f2cc0ab1f.jpg)

**3\. What was the most difficult part, and what part did you spend a lot of time on to complete this artwork?**

The most difficult part had to be making the glass bottles and vials. It’s not something I thought I’d be doing initially. It took time figuring out which pattern shapes would give the best overall bottle shape.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a404fc144f9e461c8f933e8ce0625a12/images/db793e59f4474c88899d4c66eda144d61b5d00a1ac684f85b9e2fcb767b27b10.jpg)

The liquid inside was done with layer clone under, combined with a velvet material. The corks kept managing to slip out which had to be checked every so often.  


  


**4\. What are the strong points that Marvelous Designer has?**

Marvelous Designer overall is fantastic but what stands out is being able to keep clean, consistent UVs regardless of how the mesh is actually simulated. In making the Shikari outfit I only had to re-position the UVs instead of unwrapping from scratch. Another thing I like is how the garment patterns can be modified any time during the creation and simulation processes. The largely non-destructive workflow is a great benefit. The animation with simulation feature is something I look forward to using in the future!

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/a404fc144f9e461c8f933e8ce0625a12/images/0c6dd18628324f8cb333b919cc301b7a76f42a6cb0194b9bb90a6f67dc6d3fce.jpg)

_Thanks for the interview and your amazing work, Shaafi Ahmad!_

## _Jaegil Lim shares his character creating workflow, from garment making in Marvelous Designer and final lighting and rendering._

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/4270453fe91e4daea857e08ede594e21/images/408dcf4a5a6948e6a7692b0d93f94bc161d7a56ed2bc43eda401517c53ff89ea.png)

# **Interview with Jaegil Lim | Swan | Freelancer Character Artist**

* * *

# **The Process of Collecting References For Swan**

﻿This artwork is inspired by Jun, Swan which comes from the 3rd hero character from the animation called “GATCHAMAN”

I chose to envision Swan wearing a casual outfit rather than reproducing the original hero costume from the animation.

The overall concept style is an image of a Korean woman in her early-mid 20s. The style is also inspired by the current trends of Jean Jacket, juicy makeup and bob hair.

# **A Workflow For Swan**

**1) Face Modelling in Zbrush**

Firstly, the model’s face was made in ZBrush. The aim of the model was to reflect a woman during her early-mid 20s.

I used a multi-channel face purchased from Texturing XYZ to work on the finer details of her face.

**2) Garment Making in Marvelous Designer**

The next step was to model the body.

I used Marvelous Designer to create a well fitting garment for Swans’ body shape.

I purchased a base denim jacket & Skirt set on Marvelous Designer Store and imported the patterns into Marvelous Designer to edit.

Some patterns were merged for convenience for further editing.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/4270453fe91e4daea857e08ede594e21/images/e0182a0616c74cd4bb81ce435a435bd9%EC%8A%A4%ED%81%AC%EB%A6%B0%EC%83%B7%202024-01-21%20175458.png)

For the next step, I edited the pose in 3Ds Max and converted it to an Alembic file then imported it to Marvelous Designer to apply the changed pose.

The picture below indicates that the costume was simulated in the pose shown.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/4270453fe91e4daea857e08ede594e21/images/043eb0819c3f4e9e9442203f222915e28bf71628e31f42f5936b655f14b30289.png)

After remeshing the patterns, each of Pose Mesh and Pattern Mesh were converted to OBJ files then imported into 3Ds Max.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/4270453fe91e4daea857e08ede594e21/images/67dee29ffa19488492955c1fa9b948f4%EC%8A%A4%ED%81%AC%EB%A6%B0%EC%83%B7%202024-01-21%20175603.png)

Substance Painter was used for the texturing process to express finer texture and fading of the denim jacket.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/4270453fe91e4daea857e08ede594e21/images/8d0aea0e7f5e4ab5946fd8e28679a233%EC%8A%A4%ED%81%AC%EB%A6%B0%EC%83%B7%202024-01-21%20175749.png)

**3) Hair Modelling**

Ornatrix was used in Hair modelling.

Based on the Guide Mesh I made in Zbrush, I made Cardmesh in Ornatrix. I used the same method for her eyebrows as well.

**4) Final Lighting and Rendering**

Pastel pink was chosen for the background to express a joyful and lively Swan.

Marmoset Toolbag was used for final lighting and rendering.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/4270453fe91e4daea857e08ede594e21/images/8925e77ffbdf44c3b65a7a1e8ab32224%EC%8A%A4%ED%81%AC%EB%A6%B0%EC%83%B7%202024-01-21%20175922.png)

# **Experiences in Marvelous Designer and Marvelous Designer Store**

I absolutely enjoy using Marvelous Designer Store to save time on pattern making.

It takes less time when I modify the purchased patterns to fit into the character than making patterns from scratch.

The cloth simulation in Marvelous Designer also enables me to have intuitive and efficient workflow.

Any changes made in the 2D window are directly reflected in the 3D window.

Another advantage of Marvelous Designer is the compatibility with a variety of 3D software such as Maya, ZBrush, and 3Ds Max.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/4270453fe91e4daea857e08ede594e21/images/5231bff209634cceb2427fb0efca5a9d%EC%8A%A4%ED%81%AC%EB%A6%B0%EC%83%B7%202024-01-21%20180039.png)

Check please for up-to-date pricing_** [(link)](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/4410742511769-License-Plan)

All new licenses will be available as subscription-only so that we may update new features, fix bugs, and improve other services more promptly. Existing perpetual licenses will continue to be available to those who have purchased them prior to the policy change, though new pricing policies will apply when new or additional licenses are purchased.

All new policies will take effect from version 10 scheduled for release in late November this year.

# **PERSONAL LICENSE**

The price of a personal license will be reduced to $39 and this subscription will automatically renew on a monthly basis. You can get a 40% discount for prepaying 12 months in advance.

![bdc9d94f401c4949bedd5b76f6abcc4e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ed03ffe524f444bf80d86d28bdab32c1/images/bdc9d94f401c4949bedd5b76f6abcc4e0e6afc9b5d604eaea226bda2b71cb9fe.png)Existing perpetual licenses can be used permanently._If a version of your perpetual license is less than 3 versions behind the latest version,_ you’re eligible for a 'Version Update' or 'License Trade' .

# **Version Update:**

Version Update for perpetual license will be available up to Marvelous Designer 12.   


# **License Trade:**

You can trade in your Personal Perpetual License for a 1 year subscription. After that, the perpetual license will be retrieved and cannot be reused.

(The eligibility and price of Version Update and License Trade are the same.)![9678ece0a60a4eb8943b457f4ac5a06b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ed03ffe524f444bf80d86d28bdab32c1/images/9678ece0a60a4eb8943b457f4ac5a06b779fe3cff39f48e997bbdabf9cda8803.png)

# **ENTERPRISE LICENSE**

Enterprise Standalone Annual($1,700) will be newly added and the price of Network Annual will be raised to $1,900.

![8a4a3eb35c9e4a75a5f88b0f5f64daa3](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ed03ffe524f444bf80d86d28bdab32c1/images/8a4a3eb35c9e4a75a5f88b0f5f64daa3957b2539e30f4e9c9c31e7a6105a3164.png)

Existing perpetual licenses can be used permanently. If a version of your perpetual license is less than 3 versions behind the latest version, you’re eligible for a 'Version Update' or 'License Trade' .

# **Version Update:**

Version Update for perpetual license will be available up to Marvelous Designer 12. 

# **License Trade:**

You can trade in your Enterprise Perpetual License for a 2-year subscription. After that, the perpetual license will be retrieved and cannot be reused.

For example,

Enterprise Standalone Perpetual x1 → Enterprise Standalone 2-year subscription x1

Enterprise Network Perpetual x1 → Enterprise Network 2-year subscription x1

(The eligibility and price of Version Update and License Trade are the same.)

![b01814c873aa48f7b218446254c64d79](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ed03ffe524f444bf80d86d28bdab32c1/images/b01814c873aa48f7b218446254c64d79deea3d68ed894a49839423d63d51289c.png)

Please note that technical support is officially available for less than 3 versions behind the then-current version.

# *** Marvelous Designer Student License**

A student license will be newly added. If you are a student, you can get a student discount for 3 years. Like a personal monthly license, the subscription will automatically renew and is priced at US$15 per month. Once you cancel the subscription the discount cannot be offered again, even if you re-subscribe. This student discount can be provided only once in a lifetime per user.

**All licenses except for Enterprise Network Offline requires an internet connection. Hardware Key(for Personal and Enterprise Standalone License) will no longer be provided.**

**  
**

# **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q. When will this new price policy be applied?**

The new pricing policy applies from Marvelous Designer 10 which will be released in late November 2020.  


**Q. I already have a perpetual license. Can I use it continuously?**

Yes, you can use it permanently unless you trade it for a subscription.  


**Q. How do I know if my perpetual license is subject to update or subscription conversion?**

If a version of your perpetual license is less than 3 versions behind the latest version, you’re eligible for a 'Version Update' or 'License Trade'. 

![c8455b5fab7847df89e454f541bca592](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ed03ffe524f444bf80d86d28bdab32c1/images/c8455b5fab7847df89e454f541bca592c51b4779d13e4032a61da21fa878ce6a.png)* Version Update is available up to Marvelous Designer 12.

**Q. Can I change my perpetual license to a subscription?**

Yes, only when a version of your perpetual license is eligible for the ‘License Trade’, you can.

If you have a personal perpetual, you can trade it for a one-year subscription. 

If you have an enterprise perpetual, you can trade it for a two-year subscription license.

Upon the trade, the perpetual license will be retrieved and cannot be reused.  


**Q. I’m not eligible for Version Update or License Trade. How can I use the latest version?**

You should purchase a new license to use the latest version. All purchases for new/additional seats are available through subscription only.

**Q. Can I purchase a personal annual license?**

Personal licenses are priced on a monthly basis, but you can select the ‘1 Year, Prepaid’ option for prepaying 12 months in advance with a 40% discount.

**Q. Will my subscription automatically renew?**

Only the Personal license - Monthly plan automatically renews. If you want to stop the recurring payment, you can cancel it on My Page easily.

If you have any further questions, please contact [**the Marvelous Designer Support team.**](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/support/contact)

The version upgrade discount for the existing perpetual licenses will be maintained.

If you have a perpetual license, you will be eligible for upgrading version up to Marvelous Designer 12, with the same price based on the current 3-versions-back upgrade policy.

Starting the release of version 10, new purchases will be available only by subscription.

Yes, the version you purchased is usable permanently, but the system support can be limited by versions.

Once we implement a subscription-only license model, we expect that we can provide seamless updates

There will be a change in pricing and it depends on the license type.

For instance, the price of Personal license will be lowered than the current price.

## _Daniel Moy demonstrates his process of creating a modern version of a character from the 1922 film Nosferatu using Marvelous Designer._

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/89ebb5f0d6304d2daa1c30426774d996/images/43b0a79cce924f269c6086484ee45f59daniel-moy-psx-20200125-194132_%EC%88%98%EC%A0%95.jpg)

# **Daniel Moy | NOSFERATU BREAKDOWN | ILM Creature Modeler**

* * *

# **Could you briefly introduce yourself and your team?**

I was born and raised in the San Fransciso Bay Area where I later studied and recieved a Bachelors degree from The Academy of Art University.

I have been in the film industry for over 16 years and over 25 film credits that showcase my experience. I have worked on blockbuster films such as Avatar, Planet of the Apes, The Hobbit, and have been a Lead Modeler on shows such as Fast and the Furious 7 and Beauty and the Beast.

Currently I am a Senior Creature Modeler at Industrial Light and Magic where we recently worked on Aladdin and The Irishman.

# **Could you briefly introduce the theme/ concept of the artwork? and why did you choose Marvelous Designer?**

This character is based on the 1922 movie Nosferatu. I wanted to create a modern-day version of this character on how I imagine he would look on the big screen. Everything on this asset was created from scratch.

A lot of thought when into the design of his costume. I wanted to keep it true to the original yet have it be a unique design to update his look. After looking at references and doing multiple concepts I figured out a look I was happy with. By using Marvelous Designer on Beauty and the Beast the movie, I realized the power of the software and inspired me to want to use it on a personal project at home.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/89ebb5f0d6304d2daa1c30426774d996/images/cd75ec4980ee4877bdcb7638504d2e0bPSX_20200128_002820_%EC%88%98%EC%A0%95.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/89ebb5f0d6304d2daa1c30426774d996/images/2cc5f19740c74359908bbeeb3d04ef17daniel-moy-nos11.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/89ebb5f0d6304d2daa1c30426774d996/images/40468884a6b34edd96bbfa3a8e603370daniel-moy-nos12.jpg)

# **Please explain what were the advantages of using Marvelous Designer.**

The biggest advantage of using this software was finding outfit patterns online and creating the costume based off of it. This way when it was fitted to the character I knew it would fit based on real world measurements. If something was not fitting perfectly it was just a matter of adjusting the pattern slightly and seeing the results updated immediately.

# **Would you recommend Marvelous Designer to other users? and why**

100% I recommend using this software for its accuracy and speed. One is able to manually move around the simulation in real time and change the density of the mesh for more detail with breeze. Being a VFX artist we are always trying to mimic the real world and make things look realistic and natural. With Marvelous Designer as part of my tool bag, I am able to achieve this very quickly and has huge advantages to use in a production environment. I have used it multiple films now and will continue to do so in the future.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/89ebb5f0d6304d2daa1c30426774d996/images/5eaf64c7ebc941eb9f4e4a138d550509jacke02t_%EC%88%98%EC%A0%95.jpg)

title: SELOME
content:
## _Michael Berhanu, a co-founder and Creative Director of ARMA shares how they used Marvelous Designer for an artwork inspired by Selome Tadesse's fantastic dress._

# **Interview with Michael Berhanu | SELOME | Co-founder / Creative Director of ARMA**

* * *

# **Could you briefly introduce yourself and your team?**

My name is Michael Berhanu, I am the co-founder and Creative Director of ARMA. ARMA is an advertising and motion design studio based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. We have been creating animated commercials and branded contents for our clients since 2015.

# **Could you briefly introduce the theme/ concept of the artwork? and why did you choose Marvelous Designer?**

The theme for the piece came from the show's host herself. Selome Tadesse is very conversational, easy going, and humble. Her being the main host of the talk show, we focussed on trying to find a way of depicting the free-flowing conversations that she brings to guests. That's when we discovered an art piece by Selamawit Gebretsadiq made for Selome below:

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/03ca14f34bc44caea0042bbf65aaa6de/images/df86f6c26151429995ff0606a64c8a618f3f2300679f4f3085fa2bd2cf83b37e.jpg)

The dress above is made up of the Amharic letters. Amharic is the official language spoken in Ethiopia. For the title sequence at the beginning of the show, we wanted to add depth and movement to Selome's dress. We thought a 3D dress with Amharic letters would be a good fit. We also thought this would be a nice way to secretly put meaningful words in the dress so that the audiences can discover them when they look carefully. For further inspiration, we looked into other contemporary Ethiopian artists who also use the Amharic letters in their art: namely Wosene Kosrof and Eskinder Mafi.

In order to work on our idea concerning the amount of fabric that was going to be used(95% of the whole animation is fabric), Marvelous Designer was our primary choice. We already had some experience working with Marvelous Designer on our past projects so we did not hesitate.

# **Please explain how Marvelous Designer was used in your artwork and what were the advantages of using it.**

The dress is made up of individual 2D pattern pieces that are sewn together at the waist of the character. Then we activated the Wind controller and positioned it at her waist so that it can blow the dress backward. We found out that controlling the wind type to a spherical type gave us better results.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/03ca14f34bc44caea0042bbf65aaa6de/images/df4901d2dbd049a78aa42f20bd14c7fbMD%20Admin%20-%20Article.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/03ca14f34bc44caea0042bbf65aaa6de/images/064948450aa44a9cb9cbcca3ed15bfcfb2ef0fa506df4c629881e3147bf9b78e.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/03ca14f34bc44caea0042bbf65aaa6de/images/08f5dddb8f204614a56fefd0506a95f94ff49dde0f8044eb9cfcbaaa08648bbe.png)

Through trial and error, we discovered that turning Gravity off gave us better results. We also added some 3D pins to give the dress some initial movement for the wind to act upon.

We found out that Marvelous Designer was faster and better in terms of quality with regards to cloth simulation compared to anything available. The 2D pattern workflow is also more intuitive compared to the traditional "modeling" of cloth.

# **Would you recommend Marvelous Designer to other users? and why?**

We highly recommend Marvelous Designer to anyone looking to do more work with cloth and fabric animation. The quality and speed we experienced by using Marvelous Designer were incomparable to anything else so far. We hope to use it extensively again.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/03ca14f34bc44caea0042bbf65aaa6de/images/7be8b75050d543cb8dde835d4ff908dadddf149e388a4394a6776bf55d64496d.png)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/3bda9deaf1684302a16e552684fe3103/images/d5af4174896047d39c890b2d15f7d928sekai_03.jpg)

# **Could you describe challenges in which Marvelous Designer was of use to you and go into detail regarding how Marvelous Designer helped to overcome them?**

I knew initially that I wanted a high level of detail in the cloth folds and bends. I knew it would take me forever to get there using Cinema 4D, so Marvelous Designer was a great solution in getting that high fidelity of cloth detail.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/3bda9deaf1684302a16e552684fe3103/images/31d1e8a432834cdc9b5fe28e04bafcedsekai_04.jpg)

# **Which features would you want to see from Marvelous Designer in future versions?**

I think the ability to animate objects or primitives to interact with the cloth (to get more control) would be helpful!

## _Hunt: Showdown Lead Character Artist Florian Reschenhofer endorses Marvelous Designer for game garment creation._

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/08f279f432064ece94e6e5f86984fb66/images/8957fd0423ca443c8f64fd5bc0e51328MD_02Cases_2.png)

# **Interview with by Florian Reschenhofer |****HUNT: SHOWDOWN |****Lead Character Artist at Crytek**

* * *

# **Can you briefly introduce yourself?**

Hi, my name is Florian Reschenhofer, I am the Lead Character Artist on Hunt: Showdown. I joined Crytek in 2011 and have been working in games since 2008.

# **In your project, what were the elements where Marvelous Designer was used?**

On Hunt: Showdown we used Marvelous Designer extensively on player characters and AI. Pretty much all the clothing in the game was created with Marvelous Designer. We also used it for certain pieces of gear, such as pouches and backpacks. Additionally, the environment/props team also used Marvelous Designer for some of their assets.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/08f279f432064ece94e6e5f86984fb66/images/f7d8cb7281e14a13835fe79613424452MD_02Cases_3.png)

# **Why did you use Marvelous Designer for these creatures?**

Hunt: Showdown started small, but even then we needed to generate a substantial number of assets in a relatively short timeframe, and Marvelous Designer proved extremely helpful in that regard. Beyond just generating individual garments quickly, once you build up an asset library, the process for adding new content gets faster and faster. From changing the fit to ripping up garments for zombies to utilizing an existing garment as a starting point for something new, Marvelous Designer allows for some pretty cool workflows and shortcuts. Sculpting drapery by hand can be challenging, and not all artists are equally skilled and/or experienced in doing it. Marvelous Designer allows for very high and constituent levels of quality to be put out by artists with varying experience levels.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/08f279f432064ece94e6e5f86984fb66/images/deaebe609f524651bac60f425936a637MD_02Cases_4.png)

# **Would you recommend Marvelous Designer to other CG artists and why?**

I think Marvelous Designer is currently the single-best solution for generating realistic garments in games. The turnaround times are quicker with than traditional sculpting, and the end-results look more natural than what could be achieved by hand. Also, the tool really puts the focus on garment design and fit, which is great from an artistic perspective.
content_description: This webpage showcases Hunt: Showdown Lead Character Artist Florian Reschenhofer’s endorsement of Marvelous Designer as an efficient and high-quality tool for creating realistic game garments.
